***WHO WE ARE BUILDING FOR***

*A solo GP in the Colombo belt running a private clinic with an attached in-house dispensary. One doctor. One to two front desk staff, mostly untrained. Seeing 40 to 80 patients per evening session. Operating entirely on paper. Managing stock by memory. No digital system. No patient follow up. No visibility into anything happening outside the consultation room.*

*This is not a hospital. This is not a chain. This is one doctor who built a small business around his medical practice and is losing money and patients every single day because of a workflow that has not changed in 30 years.*

*Our beachhead: Grandpass, Maligawatte, Maradana, Kolonnawa, Kotahena, Aluthkade. We have 188 verified ICP clinics within 5km. This is where we start. This is where we win before we go anywhere else.*

---

# THE PROBLEMS WE FOUND

*I spent time inside these clinics as a patient. Not as a founder. As a patient. This is what I saw.*

*Problem 1: The Dispensary Runs on Handwriting and Memory*

*The doctor writes a prescription. The dispenser reads it, re-enters the information, packs the medicines, and handwrites a label on every packet. The same information written twice by two people under pressure with a queue watching. No system connecting them. No automation. Just handwriting passed through a hole in the wall and a dispenser doing everything from memory. That is where the queue breaks, the errors happen, and the patient experience falls apart before they even reach the counter.*

*What it hurts: Queue length. Patient experience. Dispensary speed. The clinic's reputation is built on word of mouth and a slow, error-prone dispensary is the fastest way to damage it.*

---

*Problem 2: The Doctor Has No Memory of His Own Patients*

*Every visit is a cold start. The doctor sees 50 patients a day, has no history on any of them, and is making treatment decisions from scratch each time. When a patient returns, the doctor doesn't know what was prescribed before, what worked, what didn't. The patient feels like a stranger every single time. That is not a relationship — that is a transaction. And patients feel it, even if they can't articulate it.*

*What it hurts: Patient trust. Clinical quality. The doctor's ability to build the kind of reputation that fills a waiting room without paid advertising.*

---

*Problem 3: Patients Disappear Mid-Course and Nobody Chases Them*

*They feel better on day 7, stop the medicine, and don't come back. The clinic has their phone number and does nothing with it. No reminder. No follow-up. No recall. The doctor earned that patient's trust in the room and then let them walk out forever. A simple message at day 8 saying "your course isn't finished yet" would bring a percentage of them back. That is recurring revenue the clinic is currently giving away for free. And clinically, incomplete medicine courses are a real risk  incomplete antibiotic courses, unfinished hypertension medicine  the doctor's outcomes suffer because the system has no way to close the loop on what happens after the patient walks out.*

*What it hurts: Recurring revenue. Patient retention. Clinical outcomes. The doctor is running a relationship business like a one-time transaction business and losing the difference every single month.*

---

*Problem 4: The Doctor is Prescribing Without Knowing What's in Stock*

*He writes the prescription from memory and experience. He doesn't know if that medicine is available, low, or expired. If it's not there, the patient gets sent to an outside pharmacy and that dispensary revenue is gone. The doctor and the dispensary are operating as two separate people making independent decisions when they should be one connected system.*

*What it hurts: Dispensary revenue. Medicine capture rate sits at roughly 50% when it should be 70% or higher. Every patient who walks out with an outside prescription is money the clinic earned and then handed to a competitor.*

---

*Problem 5: Phone Numbers Sitting in a Drawer Doing Nothing*

*Every patient's name, phone number, age, and date of birth is written in a paper file. That file goes into a drawer. The phone number is never used. No follow-up call. No refill reminder. No appointment recall. The doctor has a direct line to every patient he has ever seen and has never once used it. That data is an asset the clinic already owns and is completely ignoring.*

*What it hurts: Patient lifetime value. Retention. The clinic's ability to grow revenue without acquiring new patients.*

---

*Problem 6: Medicines Expiring with No One Watching*

*Nobody is systematically tracking expiry dates in the dispensary. The dispenser is doing mental math across hundreds of medicines while managing a live queue. Near-expiry stock sits on the shelf until someone notices or until it is too late. There is no alert. No dashboard. No early warning. Just the hope that someone catches it before a patient receives an expired medicine or before the wastage hits the finances.*

*What it hurts: Patient safety. The doctor's legal exposure. Stock wastage that comes directly off the bottom line with no visibility until the damage is done.*

---

*Problem 7: The Lab and the Clinic are Two Separate Islands*

*Some clinics have an in-house lab. The doctor writes a test request on paper. The patient walks to the lab. The lab registers them from scratch — name, phone number, details the clinic already has — runs the test, prints the digital result on paper, and hands it back to the patient to carry to the doctor. A digital result becomes paper. The patient is the courier. If they lose it, the result is gone. The lab and the clinic share the same building but operate with zero connection. The doctor is making treatment decisions without complete information because the patient's history never travels with them.*

*What it hurts: Clinical continuity. Patient experience. The doctor's ability to deliver quality care when half the picture is missing.*

---

# THE CORE PROBLEM WE SOLVE IN YEAR 1

*Everything above is real. Everything above needs solving. But we cannot solve everything at once and win. Startups that try to solve everything solve nothing.*

*The core problem is this:*

*The Sri Lankan GP clinic has no system connecting the doctor to his dispensary, his patients, or his stock. Every evening session runs on handwriting, memory, and paper files. The doctor sees patients without context. The dispensary operates without information. Patients walk out and disappear. Revenue leaks at every step and nobody is watching it happen.*

*We solve the connection problem in Year 1\. The doctor's prescription reaches the dispensary in real time. The patient's history travels with them. The stock is visible before the prescription is written. The phone number gets used. That connection is what everything else is built on.*

# THE SOLUTION

*ClinKare connects the doctor's prescription to the dispensary counter in real time. That is the product. Everything we build in Year 1 serves that one connection.*

***Feature 1: Digital Prescription to Dispensary Screen (Launch)***  
 *The doctor selects medicines on a tablet. The moment he confirms, the dispensary screen updates instantly with the patient name, medicines, and dosage. The dispenser sees it before the patient stands up. No paper through the hole. No handwriting to misread. No re-entering data. The dispensary starts preparing before the patient arrives at the counter.*

***Feature 2: Auto-Printed Dispensary Labels (Launch)***  
 *The system generates a printed sticky label for every medicine. Patient name, medicine name, dosage, timing. The dispenser sticks it on the packet. 30 seconds per patient instead of 4 minutes. This is where the queue gets cut.*

***Feature 3: Real Time Stock Visibility (Launch)***  
 *The doctor sees live stock levels while writing the prescription. If a medicine is out of stock the system flags it before the prescription is confirmed. The doctor adjusts in real time. Fewer patients walk out with an outside prescription. The dispensary captures more revenue per patient.*

***Feature 4: Expiry Alerts (Month 2\)***  
 *The system tracks medicine expiry dates and alerts the dispenser 30 days before any medicine expires. Simple. Passive. No effort from the dispenser. Eliminates the expiry risk without adding work.*

***Feature 5: Basic Patient Records (Month 3\)***  
 *Name, phone number, age, DOB, visit history, prescriptions issued. Digital. Searchable. When a returning patient arrives, the doctor pulls up their file in 5 seconds. No paper file. No asking the front desk to dig through a drawer. The doctor walks into every consultation with context.*

***Feature 6: WhatsApp Medicine Reminders (Month 3\)***  
 *Using the phone numbers already collected, the system sends a WhatsApp message to the patient on day 8 of a 10-day medicine course. "Your medicine course ends in 2 days. Please visit the clinic to continue your treatment or call us on \[number\]." One message. Automated. No effort from the front desk. This directly attacks the patient dropout problem and pulls recurring revenue back to the clinic.*

***Lab Integration: On the Roadmap***  
 *We have seen the lab problem firsthand. The doctor writes on paper, the lab registers the patient from scratch, the result prints on paper and travels back with the patient. A digital result becomes paper. The clinic and the lab share the same building and operate as strangers. We have documented this. It gets built when the core is proven.*

---

# WHAT WE ARE NOT BUILDING IN YEAR 1

*Lab integration. Insurance billing. Multi-branch management. Patient mobile app. Appointment booking system. AI clinical decision support. IPD or bed management. Telemedicine.*

*Every request outside the six features above gets logged and moved to Year 2\. We tell the doctor it is coming. We do not build it now. Focus is the only reason startups survive Year 1\.*

# THE PITCH

*We never pitch technology. We never say HIMS, EMR, or digital transformation. Those words mean nothing to a doctor who has 60 patients arriving in 2 hours.*

*We pitch one thing: what your clinic looks like when it is running the way it should.*

***The opening line when we walk into a clinic:***

*"Doctor, imagine every patient who walks out of your clinic already has their next visit scheduled in their head. Your dispensary is running without you having to think about it. Your stock is managed. Your medicines are not expiring on the shelf. And when a patient comes back, you already know who they are, what you gave them last time, and what worked. That is what ClinKare does. Takes 10 minutes to show you."*

***The demo: one flow, nothing else***

*Doctor selects medicines on tablet. Dispensary screen updates instantly. Label prints. Done. We do not show patient records. We do not show stock reports. We do not show dashboards. We show the one thing that made the doctor lean forward.*

*Then we ask: "How are you doing this right now?" We let them talk. We listen. Then we say: "That is exactly what we replace."*

***The close:***

*"We are onboarding 10 founding clinics in Colombo. You get 3 months free, then LKR 3,500 per month locked in for life. That is less than half of what DocPP charges and DocPP's users still complain about the same dispensary problem. In return I need your honest feedback and one 2-minute video after the first month. Can we start this week?"*

***Objection: We already have a system***

*"What system are you on? How is the dispensary flow working for you?" Let them answer. If they are on DocPP: "Their own users say the dispensary is still a bottleneck. Ours is not. Let me show you the difference in 10 minutes."*

***Objection: We are fine with paper***

*"Totally understand. Let me ask you something — when a patient finishes their medicine and needs a refill, does your clinic reach out to them or do they have to remember to come back themselves? Because in 2026 every other service they use is already sending them reminders. Their bank. Their pharmacy down the road. Even their supermarket. ClinKare makes your clinic do the same thing. Automatically. No extra work from you or your staff."*

***Objection: Price***

*"3,500 a month. Right now you have medicines sitting on your shelf with expiry dates nobody is watching. You have patients who bought their first 10 days from you and spent the next 20 days at a pharmacy down the road. You have phone numbers in a paper file that have never once been used to bring a patient back. That is revenue your clinic already earned and never collected. ClinKare collects it for you. And the first 3 months are completely free."*

# GO TO MARKET: FIRST 3 MONTHS

***Month 1: Validate and Fix***

*Week 1 and 2: Get one known doctor on the product. Personal contact. Someone forgiving of friction. Sit in that clinic, watch every step, document every moment of confusion. Fix only what would kill a demo. Nothing else.*

*Week 2 onwards: Build brand in parallel. Register clinkare.com. Lock social handles on TikTok, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, WhatsApp Business. Get a logo. Print 50 one-pagers for in-person demos.*

*Week 2 to 4: Visit first 20 doctors personally. Contacts and referrals only in Month 1\. No cold calls yet. Show the 10-minute demo. Recruit 5 founding clinics.*

*Content: Post 3 times per week on TikTok and Facebook. Educate doctors on why a slow dispensary is a revenue problem and a reputation problem. Show face. Speak Sinhala for at least half the content. No heavy production. Phone camera is fine.*

---

***Month 2: Founding Clinics and Cold Outreach***

*Onboard the 5 founding clinics. Be personally present at every setup. Train the dispenser, not just the doctor. The dispenser is the one using the system 80% of the time.*

*Add expiry alerts (Feature 4).*

*Start calling unknown clinics from the verified CSV list. Call between 10AM and 12PM. Talk to the front desk. Ask for a 10-minute slot with the doctor. Script: "We have a system that connects your doctor's prescription to your dispensary counter in real time. Printed labels, live stock, patient records. No more handwriting. No more re-entering data. Takes 10 minutes to show. When is the doctor free?"*

*Brief 5 pharma reps. LKR 2,000 per clinic that activates and pays Month 1\. Give them a referral card with the product name and WhatsApp number. They mention it casually. They do not demo.*

*Target: 10 founding clinics live by end of Month 2\.*

---

***Month 3: Referral Engine and Product Depth***

*Go back to founding clinics. Bring a small gift. Ask for a 2-minute feedback video on their phone. Candid and unscripted. Ask for 2 to 3 doctor referrals.*

*Launch the referral offer: refer a colleague who activates and get 1 month free added to your account.*

*Add basic patient records and WhatsApp medicine reminders (Features 5 and 6).*

*First 5 founding clinics should now have enough usage data to show real numbers. Labels printed per session. Dispensary capture rate before and after. Revenue impact estimate. That data becomes the sales pitch for every clinic from Month 3 onwards.*

*Target: 20 paying clinics by end of Month 3\.*

---

***HOW WE MEASURE SUCCESS***

*Two numbers. Nothing else.*

*Dispensary labels printed per session: target 80% of patients per session within the first 30 days of a clinic going live. This is the adoption signal. A clinic printing labels for 80% of patients is embedded in the workflow. A clinic printing for 20% is at risk of churning. Every product decision either moves this number or it does not. If it does not, we do not build it.*

*Dispensary capture rate: from 50% to 70% within 60 days of a clinic going live. This is directly more money in the doctor's pocket. This is our retention story.*

*Secondary: 20 paying clinics by end of Month 3\. LKR 70,000 monthly recurring revenue. 10 referral leads generated from founding clinics.*

# DOCTOR OUTREACH STRATEGY

Reaching a Sri Lankan GP is not like reaching a normal business owner. He is ego-driven, time-poor, and protected by a front desk that has no incentive to let you through. He does not answer unknown numbers. He does not respond to cold messages. And during his evening session he has 60 patients waiting and zero patience for anything that is not about those patients.

The window is weekday mornings. Between 9AM and 12PM the clinic is quiet, the doctor is present, and the front desk is not under pressure. That is when every outreach method below activates. Outside that window you are wasting your time.

To get 20 paying clinics we need to reach 50 to 100 doctors. No single method gets us there. Every method below runs in parallel.

---

**Method 1: Direct Walk-In During Morning Hours**

Walk in between 9AM and 12PM on a weekday. Talk to the front desk first, not the doctor. Do not pitch. Say: "I'm working with clinics in this area on something that helps the dispensary run faster. I'd love 5 minutes with the doctor when he has a moment."

The front desk is the gatekeeper. Bring something small — a box of biscuits, a notepad with the clinic name printed on it. Nothing expensive. Just enough to be remembered. If the doctor is available you get your 5 minutes. If not, leave a one-pager and come back the next morning.

The approach: you are not selling. You are a young founder who is genuinely curious about how their clinic runs. Doctor ego works in your favour here. They love talking about their practice to someone who listens without interrupting. Let them talk. Ask questions. Then show the demo.

Target: 5 walk-ins per day, 5 days a week. 20 walk-ins per month minimum.

---

**Method 2: The Patient Approach**

Walk in as a patient. Pay the consultation fee. Go through the full consultation. At the end say: "Doctor, I have to be honest with you. I'm a founder building a system for clinics like yours. I came as a patient because I wanted to see the real experience before I approached you. Can I show you something for 2 minutes before I leave?"

You have already paid. He has already seen you as a patient. His guard is down. The honesty at the end is disarming. Most doctors will give you the 2 minutes because you respected their time enough to pay for it.

Reserve this for your top 10 to 15 priority clinics. The ones with the highest patient volume, the most visible dispensary operation, and the strongest word of mouth reputation in their area. These are the founding clinics you most want. Pay what it takes to get in front of them.

---

**Method 3: Medical Rep Network**

Medical reps visit every clinic on your list every single week. They have the relationships, the access, and the timing. The doctor sees them regularly and trusts them enough to let them through the door. That trust is what you are borrowing.

Brief 10 to 15 reps covering the Colombo belt in one 30 minute session. Give each of them a referral card with your WhatsApp number and a QR code linking to a 60 second demo video. Pay LKR 2,000 per clinic that activates and completes Month 1\. They do not demo. They do not pitch. They say: "There's a young founder building something for clinic dispensaries. Doctors I've mentioned it to found it interesting. Here's his number."

That warm introduction from a trusted face is worth more than any cold call you will ever make.

Target: 5 activated referrals from the rep network by end of Month 2\.

---

**Method 4: Medicine and Equipment Suppliers**

Suppliers visit clinics to restock medicine and deliver equipment. They have deeper relationships than reps because money changes hands directly between them and the clinic. A supplier who vouches for you carries serious weight.

Approach 3 to 5 Colombo-based medicine suppliers. Offer them a co-branded one-pager — "ClinKare, recommended by \[Supplier Name\]." When they deliver stock they leave it on the dispensary counter. No pitch needed from them. The supplier's name on the material does the work.

If a supplier is willing to mention it verbally during their delivery visit, even better. Offer LKR 2,000 per activated clinic for any supplier willing to do this.

---

**Method 5: The Clinic Neighbor Strategy**

When a clinic goes live, immediately map every clinic within 500 meters. Walk into each one the following morning and say: "Dr. \[Name\] at \[Clinic Name\] down the road just started using ClinKare. I thought I'd come introduce myself."

A named neighbor is the strongest social proof in a small community. Doctors in the same area know each other. They compare notes. If one of them is doing something the others are not, they notice and they ask questions. Every founding clinic you activate should unlock 3 to 5 neighbor conversations immediately.

This method costs nothing and scales automatically with every new clinic you onboard.

---

**Method 6: Doctor WhatsApp Groups**

Every area in Colombo has doctor WhatsApp groups — alumni networks, area medical officer groups, GMOA community pages. You cannot get into these directly. Your founding clinic doctors can.

Once you have 2 to 3 founding clinic doctors who are happy with the product, ask them to share one piece of your educational content in their doctor groups. Not a product pitch. Just: "This video explains something I deal with every day in my clinic — thought you'd find it interesting."

One share in a 50 person doctor WhatsApp group is 50 warm impressions at zero cost. This is why the founding clinic relationship matters beyond just the subscription revenue.

Activate this in Month 2 once founding clinic doctors have enough experience with the product to share it with genuine conviction.

---

**Method 7: Facebook Doctor Communities**

Sri Lankan doctors are heavily active in Facebook groups — alumni communities, specialist groups, area practitioner networks. You can post directly in these groups without needing an introduction.

Post one genuinely useful piece of content per week. Not about ClinKare. About the problems — dispensary revenue leakage, patient dropout, stock management, what modern clinic software should do. Build name recognition before you pitch anything. When doctors see your name and your content consistently they will come to you. Inbound leads from Facebook communities convert faster than any cold outreach because the doctor already knows who you are before you walk in.

Start this on day one. It takes 60 days to build momentum so the earlier you start the earlier it pays off.

---

**Method 8: Locum Doctor Network**

Locum doctors fill in at multiple clinics regularly. A single locum doctor moves between 5 to 10 clinics and sees the operational problems at every one of them. They talk to the permanent doctors. They have inside access and inside credibility.

Find 5 to 10 locum doctors through medical school networks or Facebook groups. Brief them the same way you brief the pharma reps. Give them referral cards. Pay LKR 2,000 per clinic that activates. They are already inside the door at every clinic they work in. They do not need an introduction.

Activate this in Month 2 after your core outreach channels are running.

---

**Method 9: Medical School and Junior Doctor Networks**

You are a recent graduate. You have access to medical student and junior doctor communities that no sales rep or pharma company has. These are the future customers and the current word of mouth engines inside the medical community.

Speak at one medical school event or post in one medical student Facebook group about AI and technology in private practice. You are not selling. You are educating. Junior doctors share content widely and they work in or know the doctors at exactly the clinics you are targeting. One well-placed post in the right group can reach 200 to 300 people in your exact target community overnight.

---

**Method 10: TikTok and Facebook Content as Inbound**

Every piece of content you post is a cold outreach that works while you sleep. A doctor watches your video about dispensary revenue leakage, recognises his own clinic in what you are describing, and WhatsApps you directly. That inbound lead is warmer than any cold walk-in because he came to you.

Post 3 to 5 times per week from day one. The first 60 days will feel like you are posting into silence. By Month 2 the algorithm has enough data and the community has enough familiarity with your face that content starts to travel. By Month 3 you should be receiving inbound inquiries from content alone.

This is not a short term outreach method. It is the engine that makes every other method easier. A doctor who has already seen your face on TikTok before you walk into his clinic is not a cold prospect. He is a warm one.

---

**PRIORITY ORDER: FIRST 90 DAYS**

Month 1: Direct walk-ins and patient approach only. Personal, high effort, high conversion. This is how you get your first 5 founding clinics. No shortcuts.

Month 2: Activate medical rep network, supplier co-branding, clinic neighbor strategy, and locum doctor network. These channels scale your reach without scaling your personal time proportionally.

Month 3: Doctor WhatsApp groups via founding clinic doctors, Facebook community content, and medical school networks. These are the channels that build momentum you cannot buy.

TikTok and Facebook content runs from day one throughout all three months.

---

**THE ONE RULE ACROSS EVERY METHOD**

Never lead with the product. Lead with the problem. A doctor who feels understood will give you 10 minutes. A doctor who feels sold to will give you nothing. Every conversation, every walk-in, every referral card, every piece of content starts with something the doctor already knows is true about his own clinic. The product comes after he has nodded his head at least once.

# Gifts and benefits

**PHARMA REPS**

They are motivated by money first. The LKR 2,000 commission is the real gift. But to make them feel like partners rather than contractors give them something with status.

* A clean printed referral kit — not a flyer, a proper folder with the one-pager, referral cards, and a QR code card. Something that looks professional enough that they are not embarrassed to hand it to a doctor.  
* A ClinKare branded pen or small notebook. Reps carry these everywhere. Every time they use it in front of a doctor it is a brand impression.  
* A WhatsApp group just for reps with weekly updates on activations. Public recognition when a rep gets a clinic to activate. "This week's activation came through \[Rep Name\]." Status matters to reps as much as money.

Budget per rep: LKR 500 to 1,000 one time for the kit. The commission does the rest.

**FOUNDING CLINIC DOCTORS**

These are your most important relationships in Year 1\. The gift needs to feel personal, not corporate. A doctor who receives something thoughtful tells colleagues. A doctor who receives a branded pen forgets you by Tuesday.

* A framed certificate — "ClinKare Founding Clinic, 2026." Doctors display things on their walls. Every patient who sits in that consultation room sees it. It is free advertising and free status for the doctor simultaneously.  
* A quality pen — not cheap, not flashy. A Uni-ball or Pilot that actually writes well. Doctors write all day. A pen they reach for every day is a daily brand touchpoint.  
* A small food gift on your Month 1 visit — a box of quality chocolates or a tin of biscuits for the clinic staff. Not for the doctor specifically. For the team. The dispenser and front desk will remember you for it and they are the ones using your product 80% of the time.  
* On Month 3 visit bring something slightly more personal. If you know the doctor has children, a small age appropriate gift. If he mentioned something in conversation — a book, a hobby — acknowledge it. This is relationship building not marketing.

Budget per founding clinic doctor: LKR 1,500 to 3,000 across the full 90 days split across visits.

**FUTURE DOCTORS — MEDICAL STUDENTS AND JUNIOR DOCTORS**

They have no money and enormous influence within their networks. The gift here is not physical. It is access and recognition.

* Free access to ClinKare for any clinic they start or work in for the first 6 months. Frame it as the student founder offer. They remember who gave them a break when they were starting out.  
* A proper talk or workshop — not a sales pitch, a genuine session on AI in medicine, building a private practice, technology for the modern GP. Bring them real information they cannot get in a lecture hall. That is worth more than any physical gift.  
* ClinKare branded items that are actually useful — a quality notebook, a phone stand for their desk, a laptop sticker that is design-forward enough that they actually want to put it on their laptop. Medical students are young. They respond to things that look good.  
* Public recognition on your social media. If a junior doctor helps you get a clinic referral or shares your content, tag them. Thank them publicly. In a community where reputation matters enormously, being publicly associated with a founder building something real carries weight.

Budget per medical school engagement: LKR 3,000 to 5,000 for the session including printed materials. Individual gifts LKR 300 to 500 per person for large groups.

# 

# People we should connect

**1\. Pharmaceutical Sales Representatives (Pharma Reps)**  
 Already in your doc. They visit every clinic weekly. The doctor sees them regularly and trusts them enough to let them through the door during session hours. Brands like Hemas, CIC, Sunshine, and smaller local distributors all have rep networks covering the Colombo belt.

---

**2\. Medicine Wholesalers and Distributors**  
 Companies that supply medicine directly to clinic dispensaries. They visit to restock. Money changes hands directly between them and the clinic so the relationship is deeper than a pharma rep. The dispenser knows them by name. If they vouch for you, you are in.

---

**3\. Medical Equipment Suppliers**  
 Companies supplying stethoscopes, BP monitors, examination tables, label printers, tablets. Directly relevant because ClinKare needs a tablet and a label printer in every clinic. If you partner with an equipment supplier they can bundle ClinKare with a hardware sale.

---

**4\. Medical Laboratory Companies**  
 Companies that run outsourced lab services for clinics that don't have in-house labs. They visit clinics regularly to collect samples and deliver results. They have deep relationships with GPs because the doctor is sending them business every day.

---

**5\. GMOA — Government Medical Officers Association**  
 The most powerful doctor body in Sri Lanka. Getting any kind of recognition or mention from GMOA gives you instant credibility across the entire medical community. Hard to access early but worth pursuing from Month 3 onwards.

---

**6\. Private Medical Colleges and Teaching Hospitals**  
 Institutions like Colombo South Teaching Hospital, Sri Jayewardenepura, Nawaloka, Lanka Hospitals. Junior doctors rotating through these institutions are your future customers. Faculty members often run their own private clinics.

---

**7\. Ceylon Medical College Council (CMCC) and Sri Lanka Medical Association (SLMA)**  
 Professional bodies that run CME — Continuing Medical Education — sessions for GPs. Doctors attend these regularly to maintain their registration. Getting ClinKare in front of a room at a CME session is getting in front of 50 to 100 GPs at once with their guard completely down because they came to learn.

---

**8\. Health Insurance Companies**  
 Companies like AIA, Ceylinco Life, Union Assurance that deal with private clinic billing. They have direct relationships with GPs across Colombo. A partnership or referral arrangement with a health insurer puts you in front of their entire clinic network.

---

**9\. Label Printer and POS Hardware Suppliers**  
 This one is underrated. ClinKare needs a label printer in every clinic. If you partner with a local hardware supplier — someone already selling POS systems or label printers to small businesses — they can bundle the hardware with ClinKare as the software. They get a new product to sell. You get hardware distribution handled.

---

**10\. Medical Stationary and Consumables Suppliers**  
 Companies supplying prescription pads, patient files, medicine packaging, labels, and clinic consumables. Every GP clinic buys from them regularly. They walk into the dispensary, not just the consultation room. That is exactly where ClinKare lives.

# STRATEGIC PARTNERSHIP: CEYLON COLLEGE OF PHYSICIANS

The Ceylon College of Physicians is Sri Lanka's premier professional body for physicians. Every serious doctor in Sri Lanka is connected to this institution through membership, examinations, or training. A relationship with CCP does not just open doors to individual doctors — it opens doors to the entire medical community at once.

This is not a sales channel. This is a credibility channel. One association with CCP is worth more than 6 months of cold walk-ins.

---

**Why CCP is the Right Partner Right Now**

CCP published a White Paper on Artificial Intelligence in Medicine in 2025\. The most respected medical body in Sri Lanka has already told every physician in the country that AI in medicine is real, relevant, and worth paying attention to. ClinKare does not need to convince doctors that technology matters. CCP already did that. We walk through a door they already opened.

CCP's 2026 theme is "Achieving Health Excellence through Person-Centred Care." ClinKare's patient records, WhatsApp medicine reminders, and real time stock visibility are all instruments of person-centred care. This is not a stretch. This is a genuine alignment that gives CCP a reason to say yes.

---

**The Events CCP Runs That We Target**

CCP runs monthly events that doctors attend voluntarily with their guard completely down because they came to learn. These are not conferences the doctor was sent to. These are sessions the doctor chose.

The Beyond Medicine Lecture series is the primary target. These sessions are specifically designed for non-clinical topics — technology, business of medicine, leadership, innovation. A talk titled "How Sri Lankan GPs are using AI and digital systems to grow their private practice in 2026" fits this slot perfectly. CCP provides the room, the credibility, and the audience. ClinKare provides the content.

Other events worth targeting over time:

The Young Physician Forum brings together junior doctors and registrars — the next generation of private GP clinic owners. Getting in front of them before they open their first clinic means ClinKare is the system they already know when they need one.

The Regional Academic Sessions take CCP events outside Colombo to outstation physicians. When ClinKare is ready to expand beyond the Colombo belt, these sessions are already doing the geographic distribution work.

The Annual Academic Sessions happen every September and bring hundreds of physicians together in one room. This is the largest doctor gathering in Sri Lanka every year. Year 2 target: a booth or a speaking slot at AAS.

---

**The Approach**

We do not cold call CCP. We send a single well-crafted proposal to their events committee framed entirely around their own published work.

The proposal says: CCP published a white paper on AI in Medicine in 2025\. We are building the first AI-powered clinic management system designed specifically for Sri Lankan GP clinics. We would like to offer a free workshop for CCP members on how AI and digital systems are practically changing private practice in Sri Lanka today. No product pitch. Pure education. We believe this aligns directly with CCP's 2026 theme of achieving health excellence through person-centred care.

We ask for a Beyond Medicine Lecture slot. Free of charge to CCP and their members. ClinKare funds it entirely.

---

**What We Present at the Workshop**

The workshop is never a product demo. It is a genuine educational session with three parts:

Part 1 — What AI in medicine actually means for a private GP in Sri Lanka today. Not theory. Not future speculation. What exists right now and how it applies to a solo clinic in Colombo.

Part 2 — The business problems every GP clinic has that technology already solves. Dispensary workflows. Patient retention. Stock management. Expiry tracking. Patient history. We name every problem the doctors in the room already feel but have never heard articulated this clearly.

Part 3 — A live demonstration of what a connected clinic looks like. Doctor selects medicines on a tablet. Dispensary screen updates instantly. Label prints. Patient record pulls up on the next visit. WhatsApp reminder goes out on day 8\. Five minutes. No jargon. No pitch. Just the reality of what a modern GP clinic can look like.

The doctors who want to know more will find us after the session. We do not chase them. We let the content do the work.

---

**Timeline**

Month 2: Send the proposal to CCP events committee. One email. One follow up call.

Month 3: Confirm a Beyond Medicine Lecture slot. Begin preparing the workshop content.

Month 4 onwards: Deliver the workshop. Collect WhatsApp numbers from interested doctors. Follow up personally within 48 hours of every session.

Year 2: Apply for a speaking slot or exhibition booth at the Annual Academic Sessions in September.

---

**The One Line Summary**

CCP gives us a room full of doctors who came to learn, with the most credible name in Sri Lankan medicine on the invitation. That is the most valuable sales environment we will ever be in. We earn it with genuine education and we convert it with a 5 minute demonstration that speaks for itself.

# The Sri Lankan Medical College Network

These are all the major specialist colleges operating under the same ecosystem as CCP, all listed together by the PGIM at University of Colombo:

---

**1\. College of General Practitioners of Sri Lanka (CGPSL)**  
 Website: cgpsl.lk  
 This is your single most important target. CGPSL is the professional body specifically for GPs and Family Physicians — exactly the doctors ClinKare is built for. Every solo GP running a private clinic in Colombo is either a member or connected to this college. They run annual academic sessions, CME programs, and regular workshops. Getting into a CGPSL event is getting directly in front of your exact ICP in a room they chose to be in.

**2\. Ceylon College of Physicians (CCP)**  
 Already covered. Internal medicine specialists. Senior doctors. Credibility channel.

**3\. College of Surgeons of Sri Lanka (CSSL)**  
 Website: surgeons.lk  
 Surgeons running private clinics. Less directly relevant than GPs but they have dispensaries and patient records too.

**4\. Sri Lanka College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (SLCOG)**  
 Private OB/GYN clinics are high volume, high repeat-visit practices. Very relevant for patient records and follow-up features.

**5\. Sri Lanka College of Paediatricians (SLCP)**  
 Paediatric private clinics see very high repeat patient volume. Parents bring children back regularly. WhatsApp reminders and patient records extremely relevant here.

**6\. Sri Lanka College of Psychiatrists**  
 Less relevant for Year 1 dispensary focus.

**7\. Sri Lanka College of Haematologists**  
 Niche specialty. Year 2 or 3 at best.

**8\. Sri Lanka College of Microbiologists**  
 Not relevant for ClinKare.

**9\. Sri Lanka College of Radiologists**  
 Not relevant for Year 1\.

**10\. College of Anaesthesiologists of Sri Lanka**  
 Not relevant for private clinic model.

**11\. Sri Lanka Medical Association (SLMA)**  
 Website: slma.lk  
 This is the umbrella body — over 130 years old, connects all doctors across all specialties. Not a college but a professional association. Getting mentioned or featured by SLMA reaches every doctor in Sri Lanka simultaneously. Long term play but worth knowing about.

**12\. College of Pathologists of Sri Lanka**  
 Not directly relevant.

**13\. Sri Lanka Dental Association**  
 Not relevant for ClinKare.

# **BRAND & CONTENT STRATEGY** ---

# BRAND FOUNDATION

**The Name**  
 ClinKare. Clinic plus Care. Two syllables. Easy in Sinhala, Tamil, and English. The name does not scream software. It sounds like something that genuinely cares about the clinic. That is intentional.

**The Mission**  
 To educate Sri Lankan doctors on how technology and AI can grow their practice, then give them the system to do it.

**The Vision**  
 Every private GP clinic in Sri Lanka running a faster, smarter, more profitable practice because of ClinKare.

**The Brand Promise**  
 We will always educate before we sell. We will always speak like a colleague, not a salesman. We will always make the doctor feel that technology is on their side.

---

# BRAND PERSONALITY

ClinKare is Rashard. A young, sharp, passionate founder who understands medicine enough to earn respect in a room full of doctors. Not a tech bro. Not a corporate salesman. The smart younger colleague who walks in, says something intelligent, and makes every doctor in the room think "this person gets it."

**Five words that describe ClinKare:**  
 Intelligent. Energetic. Trustworthy. Relatable. Forward-thinking.

**Five words ClinKare never is:**  
 Corporate. Stiff. Salesy. Complicated. Generic.

---

# BRAND VOICE

The tone is "වෛද්‍යවරුනි" — respectful but warm. Peer level. Like a smart younger colleague addressing the room. Not formal enough to feel distant. Not casual enough to feel unqualified.

In English: Clear, confident, no jargon. Short sentences. Direct points.

In Sinhala: Natural spoken Sinhala, not written formal Sinhala. The way you would talk to a doctor you respect but are not intimidated by.

In Tamil: Same energy. Respectful peer tone. Used when targeting Tamil-speaking GP communities in Colombo 13, Kotahena, and Grandpass belt.

**What we say:**  
 Facts about the problem. Real numbers. Real workflows. Real pain points doctors feel but have never heard articulated clearly.

**What we never say:**  
 "Revolutionary." "Game-changing." "Disruptive." "State of the art." Any word that sounds like a brochure.

---

# POSITIONING

ClinKare is not a software company that sells to doctors.  
 ClinKare is the company that educated Sri Lankan doctors on technology and AI, then built the system they asked for.

That positioning makes us impossible to copy. A competitor can copy our features. They cannot copy two years of educational content that made every doctor in Colombo trust Rashard before they ever heard the product name.

# Against competitors — indirect positioning:

We never name DocPP, BISTEC, or MocDoc. We educate doctors on what a modern clinic system should do. We show what good looks like. When a doctor is on a bad system, they will figure it out themselves. Our job is to raise the standard in their mind, not attack the competition by name.

Example: Instead of "DocPP has a dispensary bottleneck" we say "Did you know the average private clinic in Colombo loses 40% of potential revenue because of a slow dispensary? Here is what a connected system looks like."

---

# TARGET AUDIENCE

**Primary: The Doctor**  
 Solo GP, 30 to 55 years old, private clinic with in-house dispensary, Colombo belt, seeing 40 to 80 patients per evening session. On paper or on a basic system. Cares about queue speed, revenue, and reputation. Active on Facebook. Starting to use TikTok. On WhatsApp all day.

**Secondary: The Dispenser or Front Desk**  
 20 to 30 years old, mostly female, medical intern or general assistant. The daily user of the system. If she loves it, she sells it to the doctor. If she hates it, the doctor cancels. She is on TikTok, Instagram, and Facebook. Content that makes her job easier resonates deeply with her.

**Tertiary: Medical Students and Junior Doctors**  
 Future customers. Building awareness with them now means they walk into their first private practice already knowing ClinKare. Content about AI in medicine, future of healthcare, and tech for doctors resonates here. They share content widely.

---

# CONTENT STRATEGY

**The Content Philosophy**  
 Educate first. Always. Product content comes after authority is built. For the first 60 days at minimum, the content is 100% educational. No product demos on social media. No pricing. No "sign up now." Just pure value that makes doctors stop scrolling.

The product sells itself when the doctor already trusts you.

**The Face**  
 Rashard. On camera. Every video. Doctors need to see a person, not a logo. The founder-led content approach is what separates ClinKare from every competitor who hides behind a brand page and posts stock photos of stethoscopes.

**Platform Priority**

TikTok is primary. The algorithm rewards consistency and does not require followers to get reach. A good video from a zero-follower account can hit 50,000 views in Sri Lanka. This is where organic growth happens fastest.

Facebook is secondary. Sri Lankan doctors are heavily active in Facebook groups, alumni groups, and GMOA community pages. Repurpose every TikTok to Facebook Reels. Same content, different distribution.

Instagram is third. Repurpose TikTok content as Reels. Younger doctors and medical students are here. Good for brand building and eventual product awareness.

LinkedIn is fourth. Post written versions of video content. Builds credibility when doctors Google ClinKare before a meeting. One post per week is enough.

WhatsApp is the conversion channel. Not a content platform. Every piece of content should drive doctors to WhatsApp you directly. That is where the sales conversation starts.

---

# CONTENT PILLARS

**Pillar 1: The Queue Problem**  
 Educate doctors that the waiting room is a revenue problem, not just a patient experience problem. Every minute a patient waits is a minute another patient is not being seen.

Example topics:  
 "Why your patients wait 40 minutes and what it is costing you"  
 "The dispensary bottleneck every Sri Lankan GP has but nobody talks about"  
 "How one clinic in Colombo cut patient wait time from 40 minutes to 10"  
 "The hole in the wall is costing you money — here is why"

Frequency: 2 videos per week

**Pillar 2: Tech and AI Education for Doctors**  
 Make technology feel accessible and non-threatening. Show doctors that AI and digital systems are not complicated. They are tools. Like a stethoscope. You learn it once, it serves you forever.

Example topics:  
 "How AI can help a private GP in Sri Lanka in 2026"  
 "5 things your clinic software should do that yours probably does not"  
 "What happens when your prescription goes digital — a 60 second explanation"  
 "Why the most successful doctors in Colombo are adopting tech right now"  
 "ChatGPT for doctors — how to use it ethically in your practice"

Frequency: 2 videos per week

**Pillar 3: The Business of Running a Clinic**  
 Doctors are trained in medicine, not business. Nobody teaches them how to run a profitable clinic. This pillar fills that gap and positions ClinKare as a business partner, not just a software vendor.

Example topics:  
 "Why half your patients walk out the door and never come back to your dispensary"  
 "The medicine refill problem — how clinics lose recurring revenue every month"  
 "Your patient's phone number is sitting in a paper file doing nothing — here is what it should be doing"  
 "How to calculate the real revenue per patient in your clinic"  
 "What a 10% improvement in dispensary capture rate means for your annual income"

Frequency: 1 video per week

**Pillar 4: Behind the Build**  
 Show the journey of building ClinKare. Rashard visiting clinics, talking to doctors, fixing problems, iterating. This builds authenticity, trust, and a community of doctors who feel invested in the product before it launches publicly.

Example topics:  
 "I visited 20 clinics in Grandpass last week — here is what I found"  
 "A doctor showed me exactly where his system breaks down — we fixed it"  
 "Building a HIMS from scratch in Sri Lanka — week 3 update"  
 "The feedback that changed how we built the dispensary module"

Frequency: 1 video per week

---

# CONTENT CALENDAR — FIRST MONTH

Post 4 to 5 times per week minimum. Consistency beats quality in the first 90 days on TikTok. Every video is 30 to 60 seconds. Subtitles always. Mix Sinhala and English across the week.

Week 1: Introduce the problem. Queue, dispensary, paper files. Make doctors feel seen.  
 Week 2: Introduce tech and AI education. Light, accessible, non-threatening.  
 Week 3: Business of running a clinic. Revenue, retention, recurring income.  
 Week 4: Behind the build. Show the clinic visits, the conversations, the real work.

Repeat the cycle. Go deeper each month. Introduce product content only after Month 2 when authority is established.

---

# ORGANIC GROWTH STRATEGY

**TikTok Algorithm**  
 Post consistently. 3 to 5 times per week minimum. The first 3 seconds must stop the scroll. Use pattern interrupts — start with a surprising fact, a bold statement, or a direct question to doctors. Never start with "Hi I am Rashard from ClinKare." Start with the pain point.

Hook examples:  
 "වෛද්‍යවරුනි, ඔබේ රෝගීන් 40 minutes බලාගෙන ඉන්නේ ඔබ නිසා නෙමෙයි."  
 "Half your patients walk out of your clinic and give their money to a pharmacy down the road."  
 "The most expensive thing in your clinic is not the equipment. It is the handwritten label."

**Doctor Community Infiltration**  
 Every area in Colombo has doctor WhatsApp groups, Facebook groups, and alumni networks. The founding clinic doctors are your entry point. One doctor sharing a video in the Grandpass doctors WhatsApp group reaches 50 potential customers instantly. This is more valuable than any paid ad.

Ask founding clinic doctors to share your content in their groups. Not to sell. Just to share useful content. "This video explains something I see every day in my clinic — thought you would find it interesting."

**Hashtag and SEO on TikTok**  
 Use Sinhala and English hashtags together.  
 \#ClinKare \#SriLankaDoctors \#ClinicManagement \#වෛද්‍යවරු \#PrivateClinic \#HealthTechSL \#SriLankaHealth \#DispensaryManagement

---

# PAID ADS STRATEGY

Do not spend a single rupee on paid ads in Month 1\.

Month 2: If organic content has produced at least 2 videos with strong engagement (comments from doctors, shares, saves), boost those specific videos on Facebook and TikTok. Budget: LKR 20,000. Target: doctors, age 28 to 55, Sri Lanka, interests in medicine, healthcare, private practice.

Month 3 onwards: Run retargeting ads to people who watched more than 50% of any educational video. These are warm leads. Show them a product demo video or a founding clinic testimonial. Budget: LKR 30,000 per month.

Never run ads on cold audiences before organic content has proven what resonates. Paid ads amplify what works. They do not fix what does not.

---

# SEO STRATEGY

Target: Doctors Googling solutions to their problems. Not "HIMS Sri Lanka" — that is a competitor search. Target problem-based keywords.

Primary keywords:  
 "clinic management software Sri Lanka"  
 "dispensary software Sri Lanka"  
 "private clinic software Colombo"  
 "doctor queue management Sri Lanka"  
 "prescription management system Sri Lanka"

Content: Write one blog post per week on clinkare.com targeting these keywords. 800 to 1,200 words. In English. Practical, useful content that answers real questions doctors have. The blog builds domain authority over 6 to 12 months.

Local SEO: Create a Google Business Profile for ClinKare. Add the Colombo address. Collect reviews from founding clinic doctors. When a doctor in Grandpass searches "clinic software Colombo" ClinKare should appear.

---

# AEO AND GEO STRATEGY

AEO (Answer Engine Optimization) means appearing when doctors ask AI assistants like ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Google AI Overview their questions.

When a doctor asks "what is the best clinic management software in Sri Lanka" we want ClinKare to appear.

How to get there: Write content that directly answers specific questions in a clear, structured format. FAQ pages on the website. Comparison pages. "ClinKare vs paper-based systems." "Best clinic software for private GPs in Sri Lanka." The more directly we answer real questions, the more AI systems surface us.

GEO (Generative Engine Optimization) is the same principle applied to generative AI search. Structure website content with clear headers, direct answers, and specific data points. AI systems prefer content that gives clean, citable answers over long marketing copy.

Both AEO and GEO are Month 3 onwards activities. Build the website and blog first. Optimize for these after content volume is established.

---

# BRAND AWARENESS MILESTONES

End of Month 1: 500 TikTok followers. At least 2 videos over 10,000 views. Doctors in founding clinics sharing content in their WhatsApp groups.

End of Month 2: 1,500 TikTok followers. At least 1 video over 50,000 views. First inbound doctor inquiry from social media (a doctor who found us without being pitched to).

End of Month 3: 3,000 TikTok followers. Consistent inbound leads from content. ClinKare recognized by name in at least 3 Colombo doctor communities. First Google search traffic coming to the website.

---

# THE BRAND IN ONE PARAGRAPH

ClinKare is the company that showed up in Sri Lankan doctor communities before it had a product to sell, educated doctors about technology and AI with no agenda, earned their trust over months of honest content, and then gave them the system they had been waiting for. When doctors talk about ClinKare to a colleague they do not say "it is a good software." They say "Rashard is the guy who actually understands what we go through every day." That is the brand. Everything else is execution.

# RETENTION STRATEGY

---

**THE CORE RETENTION PROBLEM**

Retention is not about keeping doctors subscribed. It is about making leaving feel more painful than staying.

A doctor cancels for one of four reasons. The product is too slow. The onboarding was too hard. The value was not visible. Or the relationship was not strong enough to make cancelling feel personal.

Every part of this retention strategy attacks one of those four reasons.

---

**THE ONBOARDING PROBLEM AND HOW WE SOLVE IT**

The biggest retention risk is not Month 3\. It is Week 1\.

If a clinic has a bad first week they will never reach Month 3\. The stock upload problem is where most clinics will die before they even start.

There is no proper stock system in any of our target clinics. No Excel. No notebook. Just the shelf and the dispenser's memory and whatever supplier invoices are lying around.

Asking a dispenser to manually enter 100 to 300 medicines while running a 60 patient evening session is not onboarding. That is abandonment.

**How we solve it:**

We do it for them. Every founding clinic gets white glove onboarding.

Before go-live we contact the dispenser on WhatsApp and ask them to send us whatever they have. Supplier invoice photos. Notebook photos. A voice note listing what is on the shelf. Anything. We take whatever they give us and our team enters the full stock list within 24 hours.

The clinic wakes up the next morning with a ready system. No effort. No frustration. No barrier.

For clinics who prefer to do it themselves we provide a simple guided stock entry screen they can fill in their own time before the first session. We stay on WhatsApp throughout.

**The invoice photo feature (Month 2):**  
 When a medicine delivery arrives the dispenser takes a photo of the supplier invoice. ClinKare reads it using OCR and AI and automatically updates the stock. One photo. Done. This makes ongoing stock management as easy as the initial setup.

---

**THE SPEED PROBLEM AND HOW WE SOLVE IT**

A doctor who has been handwriting prescriptions for 15 years has muscle memory that is faster than any touchscreen. If ClinKare slows him down even slightly he will reject it on day 3\.

The consultation is intimate. Less than 1 meter between doctor and patient. The patient watches every move. A doctor looking at a tablet loses presence. Older doctors especially resist this.

**How we solve it:**

Three prescription input modes. Doctor chooses. No pressure.

Mode 1: Quick Tap Buttons. The 20 to 30 medicines the doctor prescribes most often sit as large buttons on his home screen. Built automatically from his first 2 weeks of usage. Tap, set dosage, done. 10 seconds per prescription for 80% of consultations. Faster than handwriting after day 5\.

Mode 2: Smart Search. Type 3 letters, instant suggestions appear. For medicines outside the top 30\. Still faster than handwriting once habit forms.

Mode 3: Finger Write. A white screen opens. The doctor writes with his finger exactly like paper. The dispenser screen shows the handwritten image immediately. Zero information lost. Zero new behaviour required.

Mode 3 will barely get used after week 2\. But its existence removes the pressure that makes doctors reject the system in week 1\. The escape route is what makes them brave enough to try the tap buttons.

---

**THE DISPENSER IS THE REAL CUSTOMER**

For doctors aged 45 and above who are resistant to change, the dispenser is the actual customer in Month 1\.

The dispenser uses ClinKare 80% of the time. She prints the labels. She checks the stock. She manages the queue. If she loves ClinKare she will protect it. She will train the doctor. She will push back when he wants to return to paper.

A motivated dispenser is the strongest retention tool we have for a resistant doctor.

**How we activate the dispenser:**

During onboarding we train the dispenser first, not the doctor. We show her specifically how the label printing works. We let her feel the difference between handwriting a label and pressing print. We make her the expert in the room.

When the doctor hesitates she becomes the advocate. "Doctor it is actually faster, let me show you." That sentence from the dispenser is worth more than anything we can say.

---

**THE RETENTION CALENDAR**

Every founding clinic goes through this exact process:

**Day 1: White Glove Setup**  
 Stock entered by ClinKare team. System ready before first session. Rashard or a team member physically present for the first session. Watch everything. Fix anything that breaks immediately.

**Day 3: First Check In**  
 WhatsApp message to the dispenser. "How is the label printing going? Any medicines missing from the stock list?" Casual. Fast. Shows we are watching.

**Day 7: First Data Snapshot**  
 Send the doctor a simple WhatsApp message with their first week numbers. Average patient wait time. Number of labels printed. Number of prescriptions completed digitally. Make the value visible in week 1 not month 3\.

**Day 14: Dispenser Call**  
 Call the dispenser directly. Not the doctor. Ask what is working, what is confusing, what slows her down. Fix anything she mentions within 48 hours. She will remember that for the rest of the subscription.

**Day 30: In Person Visit**  
 Visit the clinic. Bring a small gift. Sit with the doctor for 15 minutes. Show him his Month 1 data. Wait time before and after. Dispensary capture rate before and after. Revenue impact estimate. Ask for a 2 minute feedback video. Casual, unscripted, on his phone.

**Day 75: Pre-Billing Conversation**  
 Free period ends at day 90\. Do not wait for the invoice to arrive and panic the doctor. Call him at day 75\. "Doctor, your free period ends in 2 weeks. I wanted to walk you through what ClinKare has done for your clinic before we move to the paid plan." Show the 75 day numbers. Let the data close the conversation.

**Day 90: First Payment**  
 Send a personal WhatsApp message from Rashard on payment day. Not an automated receipt. A real message. "Doctor, thank you for being one of our founding clinics. Your support means everything to us. Here is what we are building for you in the next 3 months." Make paying feel like joining something, not buying something.

**Month 6: Loyalty Recognition**  
 Share their success story (with permission) on ClinKare social media. Tag the clinic. The doctor becomes a mini celebrity in the doctor community. Nobody cancels after that.

**Month 12: Annual Plan Offer**  
 Offer LKR 35,000 per year instead of LKR 3,500 per month. Two months free effectively. Most doctors will take it. Annual plans reduce churn to near zero because the doctor has already committed for the year.

---

**THE FOUNDING CLINIC WHATSAPP GROUP**

Create a private WhatsApp group with all 10 founding clinic doctors and dispensers. Call it "ClinKare Founding Clinics."

Post in it 3 times per week:  
 Monday: A tip or trick to get more out of the system.  
 Wednesday: A win from one of the founding clinics. "Dr Shivanthan's clinic cut wait time to 8 minutes this week."  
 Friday: A sneak peek of an upcoming feature.

When doctors see peers succeeding they stay. When they feel part of a community they stay. When they get early access to features they stay.

Nobody wants to leave a group where they are getting value and recognition.

---

**THE ONE NUMBER THAT PREDICTS CHURN**

It is not revenue. It is not logins. It is this:

How many dispensary labels is the clinic printing per session?

If a clinic sees 60 patients per evening and prints 55 labels per session across 5 sessions per week, that clinic is not cancelling. Ever. The product is too embedded.

If a clinic sees 60 patients and prints 20 labels per session, that clinic is at risk. The dispenser is still partially on paper. Something is wrong. Find out what and fix it before Month 3\.

Check this number for every founding clinic every week. It is the earliest possible warning signal for churn.

---

**WHAT MAKES LEAVING PAINFUL**

After 3 months of active use a founding clinic has:

3 months of patient records inside ClinKare. Going back to paper means losing that history.

A dispenser who has forgotten how to handwrite labels under pressure. Muscle memory works both ways.

A doctor whose quick tap button list is perfectly calibrated to his prescription habits. Starting over on paper feels like a regression.

A queue that runs in 10 minutes. Going back to 40 minutes is not just inconvenient. It is embarrassing in front of patients who have noticed the improvement.

A relationship with Rashard who has visited the clinic, fixed problems personally, and made the doctor feel like a partner not a customer.

None of that is transferable to another system. That is retention built into the product, the data, the habit, and the relationship simultaneously.

---

**THE ONE LINE RETENTION STRATEGY**

Make ClinKare so embedded in the daily workflow, so visible in its value, and so personal in its relationship that cancelling feels like giving something up rather than stopping a payment.
